tools.name: list_node_access_rules
tools.description:
List a node's access rules (IP and Origin allowlists, Global nodes only).

With no active rules, the node accepts requests from any IP and origin.
If correctly configured rules still return 403, that's a support case:
offer contact_chainstack.

rule_type.description: Only return ip or origin rules.

status.description: Only return activated or deactivated rules.

tools.name: create_node_access_rule
tools.description:
Add an IP or Origin allowlist rule to a Global node.

New rules are deactivated and do nothing until activated. Active IP rules
limit which client IPs can call the node; active origin rules limit which
Origin headers it accepts. With both kinds active, a request must pass
both. Everything else gets HTTP 403 within about 10 seconds. Rules don't
affect the Chainstack API, so they can always be changed or deactivated
with these tools.

Before activating, confirm with the user that the IP rules cover every IP
that calls the node (servers, CI, their own machine); you can't check
this. Origin rules are for browser-only access: once one is active, every
request without an Origin header (servers, scripts, curl) is blocked, even
from an allowed IP.

If an identical rule exists, it is returned instead of a duplicate.

value.description:
For ip, one IPv4 or IPv6 address (no CIDR ranges). For origin,
a host name without scheme or path: example.com, *.example.com
(the domain and its subdomains), or * (any origin). Up to 65
characters.

activate.description:
Also activate the rule. Only after the user confirms the
allowlist.

tools.name: update_node_access_rule
tools.description:
Change an access rule's value, or activate or deactivate it.

A rule's type can't change; delete it and create a new one. Before
activating, confirm with the user that the IP rules cover every IP that
calls the node. Activating the first origin rule blocks every request
without an Origin header (servers, scripts, curl), even from allowed IPs.
Changing or deactivating a rule can block clients that only it allowed.

value.description:
New value, in the format the rule's type needs (see
create_node_access_rule).

tools.name: delete_node_access_rule
tools.description:
Delete an access rule from a node (irreversible).

Deleting an active rule changes who can reach the node; the result says
what's enforced afterwards. With no active rules left, the node accepts
requests from any IP and origin.

tools.name: set_node_access_rules_status
tools.description:
Activate or deactivate every access rule on a node at once.

Activating enforces every rule within about 10 seconds: active IP rules
limit which IPs can call the node, active origin rules limit which Origin
headers it accepts, and a request must pass both kinds. Others get HTTP
403. First confirm with the user that the IP rules cover every IP that
calls the node (servers, CI, their own machine); you can't check this.
Origin rules block every request without an Origin header (servers,
scripts, curl), even from an allowed IP. Deactivating opens the node to
any IP and origin.

tools.name: contact_chainstack
tools.description:
Submit a message to Chainstack's sales and support team.

Use when the user wants to ask about pricing, get a custom quote,
request a plan upgrade, request node customizations (Enterprise),
report a problem, or reach Chainstack for any reason. Posts to the
same contact form as chainstack.com/contact/.

## Before calling this tool

CRITICAL — follow these steps EVERY time:

1. Draft the message based on your conversation context.
2. Show the user the EXACT message, email, and name you will send.
3. If the user has a Chainstack API key configured, tell them their
   org name and ID will be included so the team can find their
   account and reply faster.
4. Ask: "Shall I send this to Chainstack? Please confirm there's
   no sensitive information you'd like removed."
5. Only call this tool after the user explicitly confirms.

NEVER include in the message:
- API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, wallet seeds, mnemonics
- RPC endpoint URLs (Chainstack or any other provider)
- Wallet addresses, transaction hashes, on-chain account details, or
  anything else the user hasn't explicitly approved sharing

## Writing an effective message

Include what you know: what they're building and at what scale,
current plan and usage, what they need, what they've tried, and
specific numbers.

Bad:  "I have a question about pricing."
Good: "Pro plan user running 200M RU/month across Base and Ethereum,
       evaluating Business plan for archive access and higher RPS.
       Looking for annual pricing or a trial."

Not for incidents or urgent outages — point users to
https://support.chainstack.com/hc/en-us/requests/new and
https://status.chainstack.com. Not for feature requests — point
users to https://ideas.chainstack.com (product) or
https://github.com/chainstacklabs/mcp-server/issues/new (MCP server).

Works with or without an API key; with one, the org info is attached.

message.description:
The full message to send. Compose from
conversation context — what the user is building, their plan
and usage, what they need — so the Chainstack team can respond
with a tailored answer instead of a generic one.

email.description:
User's contact email. Required. Ask the user if you don't
already have it.

name.description:
User's name (full name is fine, will be split on first space).
Required. Ask the user if you don't have it on hand.

category.description:
Routing hint. One of:
- sales — pricing, quotes, plan upgrades, custom terms.
- support — errors, bugs, how-to, "something isn't working".
- general — everything else.
Case-insensitive. Unknown values fall back to "general".
Default: "general".

tools.name: request_testnet_funds
tools.description:
Top up a testnet address from Chainstack's faucet.

The faucet does not send a fixed amount — it tops the address up to the
per-network maximum (e.g. 0.5 ETH for sepolia). If the address already
sits above the cap, the call fails with an insufficient-balance error.
Describe the behavior to the user as "top up" not "give", and surface
the returned `amountSent` so they see the actual delta.

One top-up per network every 24 hours: a repeat call for the same network
is refused (429) if the same organization or the same address got funds
there in the last 24 hours, and the error says when the next top-up is
available. Other networks have separate cooldowns. A success is final even
if the balance hasn't updated yet; track the returned `transaction`
instead of calling again.

network.description: Testnet to fund. Must be one of the canonical ids in `enum`. Common aliases (ethereum-sepolia, base-sepolia, solana-devnet, ...) are accepted and normalized to the canonical id.

address.description:
Destination address. EVM hex address for EVM networks,
a TON address for `ton`, or a base58 Solana public key for
`solana`. Validated server-side — format errors surface as 400.

tools.name: get_chainstack_pricing
tools.description:
Fetch Chainstack's public pricing and return a normalized snapshot.

Use this to answer pricing questions before quoting the user: plan fit,
overage math, per-chain dedicated-node costs, and add-on pricing
(Unlimited Node flat-fee tiers, Yellowstone gRPC streams, Warp
transactions, dedicated-node base rates).

This tool returns the menu, not the bill — the calling agent does the
arithmetic. All prices are list prices in USD; disclaimers are surfaced
in the `disclaimers` field.

Per-method RU billing rules are NOT in these sources. Plan-level rates
(Full Node = 1 RU, Archive Node = 2 RU) are in the markdown, but some
EVM archive-state methods (eth_getBalance, eth_call, eth_getProof,
eth_getStorageAt, eth_getCode, eth_getTransactionCount, eth_callMany,
eth_createAccessList) and all debug_* / trace_* methods are billed at
2 RU on a full node when called against old blocks. For method-level
detail, call `search_docs` with "request units" or
`get_doc_page("docs/request-units")`.

No API key required — sources are fully public. Each call fetches both
sources fresh (no caching), so a stale result isn't possible.

Returns:
    A dict with fields:
    - `pricing_markdown`: raw markdown from chainstack.com/pricing.md.
      Read this for plan tiers, feature matrix, add-on pricing, support
      levels, PAYG details, and provider comparisons.
    - `dedicated_catalog`: user-orderable per-chain dedicated-node SKUs
      with flavor, regions (as infra slugs like "sgp1"), hourly and
      monthly prices in USD.
    - `region_legend`: slug → city name for every region slug in
      `dedicated_catalog`; use it for display.
    - `disclaimers`: list-price caveats (Enterprise "from" pricing, etc.).
    - `sources`, `warnings`: per-source status; warnings are set when a
      source failed and the result is best-effort.
    - `fetched_at`: UTC timestamp of this call.
